system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s assertions that positions are “FINAL”, “market standard” or agreed at principal level are unsupported and do not override the Buyer playbook or required Amelia Frost approvals.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | 20% of price / **AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m** for general Warranty Claims. | **Reject and counter at 25%** — 20% is an approval-dependent fallback, and Amelia Frost has not authorised it for this draft. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with only the excess recoverable. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000 tipping basket**, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject and restore Buyer thresholds** — the Seller’s thresholds materially suppress valid claims and convert the agreed tipping structure into a deductible. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notice within 18 months; limitations potentially apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24 months** for general Warranty Claims, without spillover into separate claim categories. | **Reject and require 24 months** — 18 months requires Amelia Frost’s written approval, which has not been given. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limit. | Separate regime: **100% cap**, at least **six years**, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject entirely** — title, ownership and capacity risk must not be diluted by the general warranty limitations. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no adequate fraud carve-out is stated. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of **all** caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert a comprehensive non-waivable carve-out** — the Buyer cannot agree contractual protection for intentional wrongdoing. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Deemed disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records. | Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed** with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope. | **Delete general/deemed disclosure** — mere document availability or discoverability does not fairly disclose an exception to a warranty. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for anything known by the Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion; no constructive or adviser-wide knowledge, and never apply knowledge bars to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. Any warranty knowledge qualifier should use named Seller persons after reasonable enquiry. | **Reject and narrowly redraft** — the provision improperly transfers diligence risk to the Buyer and defeats the disclosure standard. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, despite no evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are met. | Before Completion, effective Bluefen consent **and evidence that all associated conditions have been satisfied**, with no deemed satisfaction merely on delivery. | **Make this a strict Completion condition** — Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and reasonable endeavours do not remove the change-control risk. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases of all security at Completion. | **Reject post-Completion release mechanics** — any deferral requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval, neither of which is presently available. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are omitted from the funds flow and described as a Seller matter; on-costs are unquantified. | A specific funds-flow line item or other clear Seller funding for the **AUD 420,000 plus all triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs**. | **Expressly allocate and fund the liability** — the bonuses are Completion-triggered and must not silently pass to the acquired company or reduce cash delivered. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; DD-010 notes AUD 180,000 open but this is not independently verified. | A broader specific indemnity covering the Ironquay/SOW3 IP ownership and transfer risk and resulting losses, while preserving the contractual cure by verified payment and effective transfer. | **Broaden the indemnity and verify the cure amount/status** — payment alone is too narrow, and the asserted AUD 180,000 remains unverified either way. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Treated as preliminary and not expected to be material; disclosure establishes no confirmed access, breach, notification duty or loss. | Preservation of logs and evidence, continued investigation, prompt written updates, cooperation and appropriate Completion protections without prejudging the outcome. | **Require an investigation covenant and reporting protocol** — uncertainty must be managed, but the current record supports no assumed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric claim. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Characterised as ordinary-course operating costs totaling AUD 330,000. | Further assessment of timing, termination rights, accrual, necessity and ordinary-course status; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction. | **Reserve the Buyer’s position pending diligence** — the disclosed material does not establish that the renewals are unavoidable, accrued or ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | General caps, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance potentially apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Separate regimes for Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities, with no hidden general-regime override. | **Redraft the limitation architecture category by category** — an “all Claims” formulation could unintentionally collapse separately negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on the DD-012 internal share register as evidence of ownership of 100% of the shares. | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrance status and authority, alongside original/certified corporate records and appropriate releases and confirmations. | **Do not accept DD-012 as conclusive proof** — a Seller-supplied internal register is relevant evidence but not independent verification of clean title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller treats Tax and IP warranty positions as settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax and IP terms expressly **open and separately negotiated**, without assuming either unlimited liability or resolution under the general regime. | **Reject deemed settlement and reserve all positions** — no agreement has been established on the appropriate Tax or IP liability package. |
=== END ADVICE ===
